response.sql: SELECT ma.player_id AS manager_id, p.death_country, COUNT(*) AS award_count, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY p.death_country) AS share FROM manager_award ma JOIN player p ON p.player_id = ma.player_id WHERE p.death_country IS NOT NULL AND p.death_country <> '' GROUP BY ma.player_id, p.death_country ORDER BY share DESC NULLS LAST, ma.player_id LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: player.player_id is unique, so joining manager_award to player does not duplicate award rows.
The country total in the share denominator is the sum of award rows for managers who matched a player and have a non-null, non-empty death_country. Excluded managers do not count toward it.
Ties in share are broken by player_id ascending, only to make the top 10 deterministic. The request does not specify a tiebreak.
